brief: Nobody in this town goes home. `routeToExit()` (~1677) walks every leaver off the frame, and the windows (`windowLit` ~2942, hash-only, per night) light on their own with no one behind them. Connect them: a share of the walkers who leave after dusk (nightF > 0.3) instead walk to a DOOR on a cached facade that has a window above it, vanish into it, and THAT window's pane lights at that moment (a small live register keyed by (sa,sb), read by windowLit alongside its hash, repainted by drawLitPanes which already runs per frame) and keeps that window's normal bedtime. The evening door (`TAP_DOOR`, `drawTapDoor`) is the pattern for a door on `drawFaceRow`; pick 4–8 doors along the lane and the courtyard's own facades, each with a window over it. Price the walk with pathHours() first — a walker who cannot reach the door before their window's own `on` hour goes off-frame as now.
successLooksLike: On a night filmstrip a figure walks to a door, disappears, and a window above it lights in the same second — visible at 1x. Over ten seed-nights at least a third of dusk leavers go to a door, and every window lit by an arrival is one windowLit would have allowed that night (no window lit that is 'nobody home'). windows-night.mjs's lit fractions move under 10%. personName says 'heading home'. The swans, while there: rest on the bank at nightF > 0.6 (cue c75) — one line in updateSwans, not a system.
avoid: Do not make windows an agent system. One register, one predicate: windowLit stays the ONE truth and reads the register. No R() in the renderer. Do not send the east's leavers (eastOpenFor) — their walk is priced out; lane and courtyard leavers only.
